name: Plant care
intro: Where watering reminders are smart and diagnoses are accurate, and where the advice is canned.

apps.title: WaterMe - Gardening Reminders
apps.verdict: A simple, free, and reliable watering scheduler that genuinely helps people with ADHD and forgetfulness keep their plants alive. It does not identify plants or offer care advice, but it does its one job well.
apps.loved: Clean interface with no clutter and accurate watering notifications that have saved more than a few plant collections.
apps.weak: No way to pick a specific watering day, and you cannot snooze a notification when the plant does not actually need water yet.
apps.whoFor: The forgetful plant owner who needs an honest reminder tool with no extras

apps.title: Seed to Spoon - Garden Planner
apps.verdict: A real vegetable garden planning tool with educational videos from the team and concrete advice on sowing and care. The main limitations are product-level: no watering reminders, poor support for large beds and containers.
apps.loved: Users grew their first harvest from scratch and learned gardening through the built-in guides and the team's YouTube support.
apps.weak: No watering or fertilizing reminders, bed size is limited, and container growing is not supported.
apps.whoFor: The beginner gardener planning traditional in-ground rows

apps.title: Plant Daddy — Water Reminders
apps.verdict: The best of the niche watering trackers: clean interface, personalized schedules, cross-device sync, and pleasant notifications. The main pain point is data loss when iCloud runs into trouble.
apps.loved: Users say this is the app that finally helped them stop killing their houseplants.
apps.weak: No fertilizing or feeding reminders, only watering.
apps.whoFor: Houseplant lovers who need a simple and reliable watering planner

apps.title: PlantNet
apps.verdict: The strongest app in this set for species accuracy in the field, with organ selection and geotagging. The core product gap: no care advice, watering, or diagnosis, and some users get IP-blocked.
apps.loved: Accurately identifies species from a leaf, flower, or fruit with high precision, including rare plants.
apps.weak: Zero care information: after identification the user has to go elsewhere for any advice.
apps.whoFor: Naturalist, botanist, or gardener who needs precise species identification

apps.title: Plant Nanny Cute Water Tracker
apps.verdict: Plant Nanny is a human water intake tracker, not a plant care app: a virtual seedling dies if the user does not drink enough. The core feature is executed well and genuinely changes hydration habits for a wide audience, including diabetics and people recovering from illness.
apps.loved: The gamification works. Users report actually drinking more water after weeks of use.
apps.weak: You cannot manually set a custom daily water goal in the free version, even though that is the only setting that matters.
apps.whoFor: People who forget to drink water and want a light, game-like nudge

apps.title: BWH Plant Co
apps.verdict: This is a shop app for ordering plants, not a care tool. Most users are happy with the quality of plants and packaging on arrival, though occasional damaged leaves and shipping delays come up.
apps.loved: Plants arrive healthy and well-packaged even to Alaska.
apps.weak: No filter for in-stock items, so you have to scroll through hundreds of listings to find what is actually available.
apps.whoFor: Tropical plant enthusiast looking for rare species with delivery

apps.title: Seedtime: Garden Planner App
apps.verdict: A strong seasonal garden planner that auto-generates tasks by crop and reschedules when dates shift. The main weakness is that planting dates sometimes miss the mark for local conditions, and the mobile interface scales poorly on iPad.
apps.loved: Automatic task rescheduling when a planting date changes saves gardeners a lot of manual work.
apps.weak: Hard to use if you have already planted something: the app is designed for starting from scratch.
apps.whoFor: Gardeners who plan their season in advance and want a structured task calendar

apps.title: PictureThis - Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The market leader in plant identification with genuinely decent accuracy on common species, but unstable on cultivars and hybrids. The key weakness is that disease diagnosis sits behind a paywall, making the free tool nearly useless for treating sick plants.
apps.loved: Accurately recognizes common flowers and trees across different climate zones, works in the field without fuss.
apps.weak: The same photo of the same plant returns different species on repeated attempts, and accuracy on cultivars is unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Casual gardeners who need quick identification without in-depth diagnosis

quotes.text:
Three days in a row, I took a picture of this plant and it gave me three different strains of what this plant is…
I know I ordered the Purple Firespike … but the app keeps telling me it's a Mexican honeysuckle or two other varieties, I can't remember.
I use this app in Belize, New England and Canada! Very accurate highly recommend
It's all AI. Even the person helping you with questions when you have plant emergency is AI. Save yourself the money and use a free app.

apps.title: Palmstreet: Buy & Sell LIVE
apps.verdict: This is a live-streaming marketplace for buying and selling rare plants, not a care app. For its actual purpose it works, giving access to niche sellers you will not find at garden centers. Moderation and buyer protection are inconsistent.
apps.loved: Access to collectible and rare species from small growers without traveling to a plant fair.
apps.weak: An algorithmic feed replaced the chronological subscription feed and now hides sellers you actually follow.
apps.whoFor: Rare plant collector looking for niche sellers

apps.title: Garden Plate
apps.verdict: A good app with plant-based recipes: attractive design and convenient sorting by diet type. Completely unrelated to plant care. No nutritional data, and some recipes are locked.
apps.loved: Sorting by gluten content and diet type works well for vegans and vegetarians.
apps.weak: No calorie or nutritional information for any dish.
apps.whoFor: Vegans and vegetarians looking for recipe ideas

apps.title: Seek by iNaturalist
apps.verdict: A free wildlife identifier with a solid database and an educational approach, but after the latest update the camera stops focusing up close and 50% of attempts fall into the "dicots" catch-all. Not designed for houseplant care.
apps.loved: Gamification through challenges and badges draws both kids and adults into learning about nature.
apps.weak: Gives no care advice whatsoever, only species identification with no watering, disease, or lighting guidance.
apps.whoFor: Naturalist and hiking enthusiast

apps.title: Gardyn
apps.verdict: The app controls the Gardyn hydroponic system and helps grow fresh greens when everything runs smoothly. The problem is that the AI assistant Kelby cannot scan its own capsule QR codes, tasks and reminders moved behind a paywall, and periodic crashes can kill a harvest.
apps.loved: When stable, the system lets you harvest fresh lettuce weekly with minimal effort.
apps.weak: The Kelby AI cannot recognize its own capsules by QR code and requires manual entry for every plant.
apps.whoFor: Gardyn device owner who needs basic system control

apps.title: Veggie Garden Planner
apps.verdict: A niche garden planner with companion planting logic and sowing schedules. Real fans use it for years to manage crop rotation. Weak spots: no automatic zone detection and an incomplete crop database.
apps.loved: Companion planting and crop rotation logic works and helps plan bed layouts for the season.
apps.weak: No automatic planting zone detection, and many basic vegetables are missing from the database.
apps.whoFor: Gardeners with raised beds or a greenhouse

quotes.text: I paid money for a garden planner to simplify the process, but now I have to go through and look up and make note of every seedtime and harvest time for my zone. Why not just have it adjust by location?
Missing some key veggies like Bell Peppers, sweet peppers, winter squash. Recommend adding all categories from a seed catalog.

apps.title: Flora - Plant ID & Diagnosis
apps.verdict: The watering schedule works and genuinely helps people with dozens of plants keep up with care. But after updates data disappears, notifications break, and toxicity information for pets sometimes contradicts itself between sections.
apps.loved: A clear watering calendar that keeps even a large houseplant collection organized.
apps.weak: The plant database is incomplete, and toxicity information gives different answers in search results versus the plant card.
apps.whoFor: Owner of 20 or more pots who needs a reliable watering planner

quotes.text: I understand this has conveyed to a paid app with a three day trial. What I don't understand is an update deleting all of my plants and progress. Deleted the app. Used it for a long time only to lose everything.
I have a Madagascar Tree (Dracaena Marginata) and in the search it says it's pet friendly but once I add it to my plants it says it's toxic to pets so which is it?
It's pet-safe toxicity information is frankly inaccurate at times. There should be a feedback information loop for users.
Over half my plants are not in their plant library.

apps.title: Planta: Plant & Garden Care
apps.verdict: The best care planner in the category: watering, fertilizing, and repotting schedules work and keep collections alive for users who treat it as an organizer. The weak spot is performance instability and excessive notifications asking for health updates.
apps.loved: Adapts the watering schedule to the specific species and season, with dozens of plants in a single daily task list.
apps.weak: The watering schedule cannot adapt to drip irrigation or non-standard routines, sending daily reminders where once a week would be right.
apps.whoFor: Owners of large home collections who need an organizer, not an identifier

quotes.text: The watering schedule is problematic as I don't know how to represent a drip system that does a deep soak. The result is I get reminders every day to water plants that should be 1-2 per week.

I have used this app for 5 years now or more. I am very experienced with my plants, so I prefer the free version. I use it to organize my plants with pictures. But mainly to keep track of the last time it was watered.

I downloaded this a while back, not thinking it would actually be of some good BUT I was totally wrong. Because of this app (and further research at a nursery), I have about 10 thriving plants and I knew nothing of gardening firsthand! This app makes me proud to be a learning gardener.

apps.title: Greg: Plant Identifier & Care
apps.verdict: The most thoughtfully designed watering tracker in this set: tracks pot size, sends reminders, manages a collection. But the identifier mixes up orchids, hoya, and mint with alfalfa, and app reliability has dropped lately.
apps.loved: The watering reminder system accounts for plant species and pot size, which genuinely helps avoid overwatering.
apps.weak: The identifier struggles with atypical specimens, and there is no way to correct a wrong identification.
apps.whoFor: Owner of 5 to 20 houseplants who needs a watering tracker

quotes.text: Watering recommendations should be based on size of the plant, not just size of the pot. FERN misses on this. Also, I think water recommendations are much too frequent for - established large snake plant and large zz plant.

I love this app. Been using it for a little over a year. I do wish it had the ability to tell it when I plant 2 different plants together in 1 pot and most importantly that my plant is still wet when it recommends watering.
I wanted to like & use this app but it failed immediately in identifying plants in my garden. For example identifying the my perennial flowering catmint plant as alfalfa and then as chaste tree.
Missed the proper ID of both my orchids and hoya

apps.title: Home Design 3D Outdoor&Garden
apps.verdict: A decent 3D yard planning tool, but completely unrelated to plant care. The object library is thin, garden shrubs and plants are sparse, and data sometimes vanishes after a crash.
apps.loved: Convenient for sketching a rough backyard or pool layout before meeting with a contractor.
apps.weak: Very few actual garden plants and shrubs in the catalog.
apps.whoFor: People planning a yard or landscape layout

apps.title: Plant Parent: Plant Care Guide
apps.verdict: An app with a pleasant interface for organizing a collection and its schedule, but the plant database is narrow: dozens of philodendron, anthurium, and alocasia varieties are missing. Diagnosis is weak: it reported a dying hydrangea as fine, and fertilizing information contradicts itself across sections.
apps.loved: Clean plant card interface with a growth photo log and task schedule on one screen.
apps.weak: The species database is outdated and incomplete for tropical plant collectors, and adding a species manually is not possible.
apps.whoFor: Beginners with a small collection of popular species

quotes.text: It's a good app. But it could be better. I have a lot of different plants and sometimes can't add them because it's not in the system. Like there are so many different philodendrons and the app only has a few to select from. Just like anthurium and alocasia and so on.

apps.title: Plant Identifier & Care App
apps.verdict: Recognition works in roughly 80% of cases for common species, and there is a useful light check and overwatering diagnosis. Disease and pest identification is weaker, especially on blurry photos or uncommon species.
apps.loved: The light sensor helped one user realize a fern was getting too much direct sun.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis is unreliable: fungal infection on lilac was not recognized at all.
apps.whoFor: Beginners with a few houseplants

quotes.text: It says my dying snake plant is healthy. Can't unsubscribe.

Saved my favorite plant. It correctly diagnosed an overwatering issue and gave a solid care schedule. Taking off one star because the photo scanner can be a bit picky if the lighting isn't perfect, but otherwise great.

apps.title: Farm Your Yard: Gardening App
apps.verdict: The concept is right: a planting calendar localized by climate zone with a task list. But recommended dates are sometimes off by a month from reality, and the app regularly loses data after updates.
apps.loved: Users appreciate that the app adapts the planting schedule to their specific region.
apps.weak: The crop list is limited, has no search, and adding a non-standard plant is impossible.
apps.whoFor: Beginning gardeners in US climate zones who can tolerate occasional data loss

apps.title: PlantSnap - Plant Scanner
apps.verdict: One of the oldest identifiers with a large database, working well on trees and wildflowers, but it consistently flags three-leaf plants as poison ivy and offers almost no care tools. Disease diagnosis is generic and unreliable.
apps.loved: Quickly identifies wild species from a photo with no preparation needed, large flora database across many regions.
apps.weak: No dedicated care or watering module, and identification in ambiguous cases is unreliable with no alternative suggestions.
apps.whoFor: Naturalists and hikers who need to quickly identify a wild plant on the trail

apps.title: PlantIn: Plant Identifier・Care
apps.verdict: An app with a built-in botanical chat and watering schedule, but identification accuracy is low: it confuses watermelon seedlings with cucumber and fails to recognize basic cultivated plants. Real harm is confirmed by users who lost their collections following its advice.
apps.loved: The ability to chat with a bot about a specific plant is handy when you need step-by-step guidance.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis comes down to five template answers (overwatering, underwatering, light) without looking at the actual symptoms.
apps.whoFor: Beginners willing to cross-check advice from other sources

quotes.text: Very generic disease identifying and care
As of the latest update, I cannot open The app. I have 150 plants and I use the app primarily for a watering schedule. I have tried everything except deleting the app because I will lose my data.
I had no idea it was poisonous. I took a picture of it and this app was so informative….

apps.title: PlantAI: Identifier & Diagnose
apps.verdict: Has a working AI chat and basic identification, but the light meter gives incorrect readings even under grow lights, and disease diagnosis consistently falls short of expectations.
apps.loved: Older users appreciate the simple interface and the AI chat for basic care questions.
apps.weak: Light meter is inaccurate, disease diagnosis lacks specific treatment steps, and watering advice does not account for soil moisture.
apps.whoFor: Beginning home gardener with a small collection

quotes.text: The plant identifier is nice, the when to water is nice, though I did discover my plants do better when I check the soil for moisture rather then go by a calendar.

A very disappointing app. There is nothing special to warrant the $30 a year price. I was hoping for a more in-depth disease diagnosis but the app gives no more than what is free when you google or ask Siri.
I know what my plants are, I need to know what problems exist and what can be done. I do not need a photographic album of them. H E L P me save my plants.

This app is very helpful for diagnosing diseases and curing plants. I like the variety of different tools that you can use, and the AI chat to get quick info about them. Though there have been a few times that the app has given inaccurate information, it is good for the most part.

apps.title: Plantify: AI Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: Identification generally works and has helped some users save plants, but problem diagnosis is fundamentally unreliable: it returns succulents instead of legumes and gives no concrete treatment advice.
apps.loved: Can be accurate on clean shots and gives specific care tips for the identified plant.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis confuses species and does not explain what to do with a specific problem.
apps.whoFor: Beginning gardener who needs basic species identification

apps.title: GrowIt: Garden Planner
apps.verdict: A garden planner with a visual bed layout and watering schedule, but weather data is regularly wrong: after 100mm of rain it still tells you to water. The crop variety database is thin, and agronomic advice is sometimes incorrect, such as squash family sowing recommendations.
apps.loved: Visual garden layout with companion planting helps plan bed arrangements.
apps.weak: Weather integration is unreliable, making the watering schedule more harmful than helpful.
apps.whoFor: Gardener who needs a visual bed layout tool

quotes.text: This app is terrible. It literally can't identify any varieties, it never knows when it's actually rained well enough and constantly tells me I need to water. The final straw was the fact we got 4 inches of rain last night and the app is harassing me to water my plants.

Water pacing is good in general terms, but there are no exceptions to it. We are in a drought right now and plants that normally wouldn't need water are droopy and begging for it. Please improve the weather feature on the app to include this type of scenario.

Overall, this app is good and extremely helpful for reminders for watering and helpful tips for growing different fruits and vegetables. I withheld one star because the weather is not as accurate as it should be to help with watering, certain varieties of plants are missing or all lumped together.
I started to enter the varieties of plants and herbs I planted and the database didn't have ANY of them. Thankfully I just did the trial because I would have been livid if I paid for this.

apps.title: Blossom - Plant Care Guide
apps.verdict: An app with a good idea for personalized care scheduling that degraded after a tripled price hike and sync failures: collections reset to zero, schedules shift on their own, and care advice does not work for non-standard climates like Arizona. AI diagnostics are superficial.
apps.loved: When the app runs stably, managing a large collection's care schedule is convenient and clear.
apps.weak: Watering schedule does not adapt to climate or pot size and shifts for no apparent reason after updates.
apps.whoFor: Users in temperate climates with basic houseplant species

quotes.text: I love this app, all except one major gap. I live in Arizona and the temperatures during much of the year are much higher than the top range in the app. Therefore the schedule for watering isn't accurate as calculated by the app. Everything has to be manually adjusted. Also many desert plants are not even in the database.

I remember when this app had a human review plant questions, and issues when submitted. Now it's AI only. Even when you submit something using the plant health feature it's strangely tells you it's reviewed by 'Kate.' I'm guessing Kate is AI generated? A bit confusing to mislead people that a human is behind it.

apps.title: Plant Identification－Plantaria
apps.verdict: Identification works fast but accuracy is inconsistent: only 5 out of 23 plants identified correctly according to one review. Disease diagnosis consistently does not work.
apps.loved: Instant photo recognition delights beginners and kids.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis is non-functional, care tips are too generic, and the feature for handling sick plants is essentially absent.
apps.whoFor: Curious beginners who just want to know a plant's name

apps.title: AeroGarden
apps.verdict: When login works, the app usefully manages the lighting schedule and reminds you about nutrients. But account login breaks regularly, schedules reset after power outages, and physical controls were removed from the device, so without a working app the plants go unattended.
apps.loved: A working lighting schedule and water and nutrient notifications make herb growing genuinely hands-off.
apps.weak: Login breaks every few months, after which controlling the device is physically impossible.
apps.whoFor: AeroGarden hydroponic device owner willing to deal with periodic login failures

apps.title: Plantum - AI Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: An identifier that once worked has degraded to near-total paywall lockdown: free identification is gone, experts take weeks to respond if at all, and the orchid and rare species database is extremely thin. Value as a care tool is close to zero.
apps.loved: The plant journal interface is convenient for keeping a photo diary of a collection, and reminders fire accurately.
apps.weak: Identification is unreliable on cultivars and hybrids, and manually correcting a result is not possible.
apps.whoFor: Users who only need a journal and reminders without identification

quotes.text: Overall, the app is great! I use it as my orchid journal. However, it lacks the intelligence to accurately identify my orchids, and the database for manual searches is quite limited in terms of orchid species.

Just stick with the basic functions of the app. It's fun to use and decently effective at giving you basic info about your plants. Do NOT give them any money though. You will just throw your money away and will never actually hear back from their 'plant experts'.

Hi there well I think it's very helpful because I can identify plants. It doesn't always work so well with deciding whether a plant is healthy or not. Sometimes I disagree however what really irritated me is that I paid $20 to have a Plant expert help me with a plant and that was weeks and weeks ago.

I just got it and it helped me fix my tomato plant and now it's growing. It also helped my succulent and now my succulent is so much better and help me diagnose that my tomato was sick and I recommend using this app

apps.title: Grow A Garden Companion Guide
apps.verdict: This is a companion app for the Roblox game Grow a Garden, not a real gardening tool: it notifies you when seeds and items appear in the in-game shop. Servers are often unavailable, and the game database lags behind updates.
apps.loved: Working notifications about rare items in the in-game shop genuinely help players not miss what they need.
apps.weak: Server is frequently unavailable, and the catalog does not keep up with game updates.
apps.whoFor: Roblox player who does not want to miss event seeds

apps.title: Plant Identifier: LeafSnap
apps.verdict: Basic recognition works and care cards and a plant collection are included. But sync is poor: data does not transfer to a new phone, and the sync process drains the battery.
apps.loved: Recognition of most common species works quickly.
apps.weak: The plant collection does not sync between devices and is lost when switching phones.
apps.whoFor: People willing to keep their collection on a single device

quotes.text: I took a lot of time to set up all of my gardens on here, including care and notifications. When I bought a new phone, nothing transferred over. So disappointing. Loved it until then.

apps.title: Plant Identification ++
apps.verdict: Identifies common plants tolerably but regularly misses trees and lesser-known species, and offers almost no disease diagnosis. After a major update, photo saving and social features broke.
apps.loved: Long-term users appreciate the broad database of garden and field plants.
apps.weak: Instead of explaining how to treat a disease, redirects to an external site with no specifics.
apps.whoFor: Casual gardener who just needs a plant name

quotes.text: Each time I use it it just sends you to a website for whatever plant it thinks it is identifying. It does not give you any hints on whatever disease your plant may have.

apps.title: Planto: Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: Identification is superficial, disease diagnosis is broken according to widespread reports, and a photo limit on the collection makes the core feature inconvenient even for paying users.
apps.loved: Quickly identifies a species from a photo and sometimes helps you confirm something is not a weed.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis does not work reliably, and the photo limit in the collection gets in the way of tracking plants.
apps.whoFor: Someone who needs to look up an unfamiliar plant's name once

quotes.text: I can't get the diagnosis part to work. I have tried every way and angle of picture I can possibly think of and it just won't diagnose.

apps.title: Plant Guru - Plant Care Guide
apps.verdict: Identification is unreliable for common cultivated plants, and diagnosis gives generic advice instead of concrete steps. Users who need help with a sick plant leave disappointed.
apps.loved: Works better for wild plants and garden perennials than for vegetable crops.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis is limited to general recommendations with no concrete actions.
apps.whoFor: People who enjoy walking and identifying wild plants

quotes.text: I paid for this app expecting the photo identification to be accurate and it's really bad. It thinks every common plant here in NY is some type of Japanese weed. It repeatedly told me my eggplant is a tomato, garbage.

I wanted to diagnose my plants with the help of this app. Instead, the app wants me to give my plants names and I guess I'm supposed to figure out what's wrong and then just keep a journal here. I paid for your subscription for the help of my plants. And now I have to diagnose them myself.

apps.title: Plant App: Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: A basic identifier with unstable accuracy: the same object gets different names on repeated shots, and coarse errors like mushroom identified as a palm have been documented by users. Disease diagnosis and care tools are nearly absent.
apps.loved: Sometimes correctly identifies common species like nasturtium on the second try.
apps.weak: Identification is unstable to the point where trusting the result without a second check is risky.
apps.whoFor: Casual users who need identification once a year without accuracy expectations

quotes.text: I took three pictures of the same tree and it gave me three different names. This app is garbage.

apps.title: Free Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: Three free attempts per day, then a subscription, and accuracy on common vegetables is below expectations. Disease diagnosis costs extra. Fine for casual curiosity, not for serious plant care.
apps.loved: Care tip cards (watering, fertilizing, light) shown after a successful identification are written clearly.
apps.weak: Three daily attempts are not enough to judge how accurate the identifier is before paying.
apps.whoFor: Casual user who needs to identify an unfamiliar plant

quotes.text: You get what you pay for. Glad this is free because I've taken 3 pictures of one volunteer tree and gotten 3 different answers.

apps.title: Plantion - Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The app's core flaw is well-documented in reviews: diagnosis almost always returns healthy even for plants that are visibly dying or already dead. Identification only handles broad families, not specific species.
apps.loved: Quickly names a plant family from a good photo.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis is functionally broken: returns healthy regardless of the plant's actual condition.
apps.whoFor: Someone who already knows their plant and just wants to confirm the name

quotes.text: The app said it will help identify and help my plant may or may not need and every picture says healthy. But I put a picture of a dead plant and it said healthy. A waste of money.

Kept seeing the ad for the app, scanning grass in the yard and identifying issues. Set up the trial, took several pictures of my dying struggling lawn that the lawn guys haven't fixed yet. Close up, far away, etc. Every picture says it's healthy.

I don't have very much success identifying problems with my plants. I take a good photo, but most of the time the diagnosis says that the plant is 'healthy'. I need a better way to identify the disease on my plants before it's too late.

I've purchased the subscription based on an advert I saw on Instagram. It was quite straightforward video how this app would recognize the plant and would give very specific advice. Instead it gave very generic advice like 'it's either overwatering or under watering' without any real specific input.

apps.title: Plant Identifier, Plant Care
apps.verdict: Identification accuracy is low: the same plant gets different answers, and a bromeliad was identified as snake plant. Intrusive ads after every scan make the experience unbearable.
apps.loved: The app is free and requires no subscription for basic recognition.
apps.weak: Ads after every photo scan and weak species recognition.
apps.whoFor: People who want to try plant identification at no cost

apps.title: Sow: Garden & Landscape Design
apps.verdict: The idea of an AI visual garden planner is interesting, but in practice the generation outputs images of a cake or a crying girl instead of a garden layout. The app frequently fails to launch, and toxic plants show up in recommendations even after explicit exclusions.
apps.loved: The drag-and-drop editor for arranging plants on a site plan is called more convenient than alternatives by a handful of users.
apps.weak: AI generation is unreliable and produces random results instead of garden layouts.
apps.whoFor: Landscape enthusiasts willing to tolerate instability for a visual planner

apps.title: Plant Identifier, Care: Planty
apps.verdict: The identifier confuses Thanksgiving cactus with Christmas cactus, consistently diagnoses any problem as needing less water, and the water all button does not actually log watering. For a beginner who loses a plant, this app is more likely to make things worse.
apps.loved: The growth journal and watering reminders are appreciated by those with one healthy houseplant.
apps.weak: Diagnosis works from a template and gives the same answer regardless of the symptoms.
apps.whoFor: Beginner with one low-maintenance plant

quotes.text: This app is definitely not worth your time. Almost every plant issue seems to get the same answer: 'needs less water.' The information it provides is very basic and doesn't go much beyond what most people already know.
The app couldn't tell the difference between a Christmas cactus and Thanksgiving cactus. They are different and they require two different types of care.
I identified the identifier works well, has a lot of cool features for example checking to see if your plant is getting enough sunlight however had a lot of trouble getting the app set up.

apps.title: Plant Identifier & Care: Ficus
apps.loved: The interface is simple and information about a plant appears quickly.
apps.weak: Recognition is unreliable even for common species.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

apps.title: Plant Identifier & Plant Care.
apps.verdict: Identification is inaccurate according to multiple users who report wrong IDs and diagnoses. The real value as a plant care tool is not supported by substantive reviews.
apps.loved: Convenient to photograph an unfamiliar plant and get at least some care hint right away.
apps.weak: Recognition is unreliable: the app confuses species and gives incorrect disease diagnoses.
apps.whoFor: Beginner who is fine with an approximate watering suggestion

apps.title: Plantora- Plant Identify, Care
apps.verdict: Plant identification works intermittently: cucumber identified as squash, rhododendron as strawberry tree. Disease diagnosis follows template questions without actually analyzing the photo, and the result is predictably vague.
apps.loved: Some users appreciate that the app is genuinely free without a forced subscription.
apps.weak: Recognition accuracy is too low for practical use.
apps.whoFor: People who want to try a plant identifier for free with no high expectations

apps.title: Plantfie・Plant Care Identifier
apps.verdict: Mistook a birkin philodendron for a calla lily, could not find a money tree, and told a user with yellow, pest-ridden leaves that their plant was healthy. The 7,000-plant database claim sounds good, but accuracy is at chance level.
apps.loved: The watering tracker with reminders is appreciated by users with many plants who cannot track manually.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis does not work and returns healthy regardless of the plant's actual state.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

quotes.text: This app you have to pay nearly $50 a month to use the diagnose feature by taking a picture. Half the time it says the plant is healthy even when the leaves are yellow and half missing from being eaten by pests.

I wish the app would tell me specifically who the plant is toxic to. Is it people, cats, dogs, rabbits, ferrits, hedgehogs, bearded dragons, sugar gliders, etc. This would greatly help pet parents make good plant choices. I would purchase the app for that because I love plants, but also have pets.

As a person that owns over 50 house plants, I wanted something that could keep the inventory easily for me. The bank of plants needs some updating to include the different variations of certain plants, not just the general type.

apps.title: AI Plant Identifier・Care－Lily
apps.verdict: Actual app functionality is barely traceable in reviews: ads promised specific home remedies, but the app only gives standard watering and light tips. Diagnosis takes up to two days and often does not complete.
apps.loved: A few users like the idea of teaching their family about plants together.
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis is slow and non-functional, with minimal real help for saving a plant.

quotes.text: The ads for this app are a hoax. Says the ad: add coffee, add milk. You know what I got for my sick plant? Information about watering and sunshine. Really? Thanks for nothing.

apps.title: Plant Identifier: Plantiary
apps.verdict: Did not recognize a sunflower, confused zucchini with a pumpkin, and got 5 out of 5 known plants wrong according to a review from an experienced gardener. No real value for plant care, and the pricing model is hidden until the last moment.
apps.loved: Occasional users like the identification interface during walks.
apps.weak: Accuracy is insufficient even for the most common garden plants.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

apps.title: Plant Identifier: ChatPlant AI
apps.verdict: Real users report that the same photo returns a different wrong answer every time, and disease diagnosis ignores visible symptoms. Boosted five-star ratings create a false picture of quality.
apps.loved: The chat interface looks modern and is comfortable for talking about plants.
apps.weak: Recognition is unstable: the same photo gives a different wrong result each time.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

quotes.text: Took the same picture and resubmitted it several times & each time it came back with a different identification , all completely wrong.
Based on online ads I thought this app would offer more detailed guidance, but it offers the same 'maybe it's this or maybe it's that' level of guidance that other apps do.

I rarely write reviews, but this app deserves 5 stars. It helped me save my struggling plants with clear diagnosis and practical tips. I no longer forget to water or overwater my green friends. Simple, reliable, and incredibly useful my go-to plant companion!

apps.title: Garden AI: Landscape Design
apps.verdict: AI yard redesign looks attractive but ignores lighting, terrain, and actual dimensions: proportions are off and elements appear where they should not. Does not work as a real garden planning tool.
apps.loved: Helps quickly show a partner a visual concept for the yard without hand sketches.
apps.weak: Generated designs ignore site-specific conditions: shade, slope, and climate zone.
apps.whoFor: Someone who needs an image to discuss an idea, not an accurate plan

apps.title: Plant Identifier - PlantMe
apps.verdict: Identifies cucumbers as zucchini or oregano, does not work with photos from the gallery, and continues charging weekly after the app is forgotten. No real value for plant care.
apps.loved: Watering reminders and diagnosis are appreciated by the few for whom the app actually worked.
apps.weak: Identification accuracy is extremely low, confusing basic vegetable crops with each other.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

quotes.text: This app is for you if you want to be in the wife's doghouse. Yes it identified one of her plants as a weed and Cut it down then she cut off my head. Identifies wrong more than right. This morning it identified my cucumbers as squash, then oregano, then yet something else.

apps.title: AI Garden Design: Landscape AI
apps.verdict: This is a landscape visualization generator, not a plant care tool: no identification, no care advice, no disease diagnosis. Generated images do not include plant names, so there is no way to turn a picture into a shopping list.
apps.loved: Helps visualize the general look of a yard before work begins.
apps.weak: Does not name the plants in generated images and gives no care information about them.
apps.whoFor: Someone visualizing a landscape, not caring for plants

apps.title: Plant & Bug Identifier
apps.verdict: Plant recognition fails in most cases: rose, petunia, and bamboo all went unrecognized, and the app returns an error on ordinary garden photos. The free database is effectively inaccessible.
apps.loved: Users note the variety of reference information about plants in the catalog.
apps.weak: The core photo identification feature regularly fails even on common plants.

apps.title: PlantLush: Plant ID & Care Pro
apps.verdict: The product has virtually no real users: nearly all reviews are about misleading free advertising. The quality of recognition and care advice cannot be evaluated because the features are inaccessible.
apps.loved: One user noted useful diagnosis of overwatering tendency.
apps.weak: Plants cannot be added manually, and the identifier lets them through incorrectly.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

apps.title: PlantDaily: AI Plant Care
apps.verdict: By users' own admission, plants are identified correctly only about 3 times out of 10. The diagnosis feature hangs, the support chat fails to send, and the app gives no care tips even after a successful identification.
apps.loved: The interface looks clean and promises useful functionality.
apps.weak: Identification accuracy is too low to trust any care recommendations that follow.
apps.whoFor: Not suitable for anyone in the current state

apps.title: Plant AI: Scanner & Identifier
apps.verdict: The app fails at basic tasks: identification does not work or takes forever, and diagnosis hangs and never returns a result. Users call it useless even for common garden plants.
apps.loved: The idea of photo-based disease diagnosis is in demand, but the implementation does not let you use it.
apps.weak: Recognition cannot identify even ordinary plants, and the diagnosis feature just spins a loader with no answer.
apps.whoFor: Not suitable for anyone at the current quality level

apps.title: FloraSnap: Plant Scanner
apps.verdict: Nearly all reviews are about deceptive pricing, and of the few users who tried the features, one got a wrong identification and another hit network errors. As an identification tool the app does not work.
apps.loved: Visually the app looks clean.
apps.weak: Recognition does not work due to persistent network errors and the feature set is effectively inaccessible.

apps.title: Busch Gardens
apps.verdict: This is the official app for the Busch Gardens theme park: park map, ride wait times, and tickets. It has nothing to do with plant identification or care and cannot be evaluated in this category.
apps.loved: The interactive park map with geolocation works on the spot.
apps.weak: Ride wait times update infrequently and do not match reality, and account login occasionally fails.
apps.whoFor: Busch Gardens theme park visitors

apps.title: Water Garden Life
apps.verdict: This is not a plant care app but a gamified ad aggregator with a watch-ads-for-rewards mechanic. Its rating in the plant care category is entirely irrelevant.
apps.loved: A reminder to drink water is the only connection to a living organism that a few users mention.
apps.weak: The app has no relation to plant care or identification.
apps.whoFor: Not for gardeners

apps.title: Better Homes and Gardens
apps.verdict: This is not a plant care app but a digital version of Better Homes and Gardens magazine. Evaluating it in the plant care category is irrelevant.
apps.loved: Magazine fans appreciate the convenient format for reading on a tablet.
apps.weak: The app periodically loses downloaded issues and does not work offline reliably.
apps.whoFor: Not for gardeners

scenarios.name: The forgetful owner with a collection
scenarios.job: Hires the app so plants stop dying from a missed watering: what is needed is precise notifications, not advice and an encyclopedia.
scenarios.gap: The reviews ask for the interval to be changed and the watering moved if the soil is still damp. The schedule has to allow for the owner’s own decision.

scenarios.name: The serious tropical plant collector
scenarios.job: Hires the app to buy rare species from niche growers and keep records of a collection of 50+ plants with a photo diary.
scenarios.gap: Owners of rare plants run into an incomplete database. A journal benefits from a name entered by hand, a photograph of your own and a care history that does not have to match the catalog.

scenarios.name: The first-time vegetable gardener
scenarios.job: Hires the app to plan a season from scratch, work out the sowing dates and not ruin the first harvest.
scenarios.gap: Authors ask for their zone and the actual start of planting to be taken into account. A useful test is adding a crop that has already been planted and correcting the dates for your own plot.

scenarios.name: The naturalist who loves a walk
scenarios.job: Identify a plant noticed on a walk and save the find; when questions of safety come up, find reference information that can be verified.
scenarios.gap: After an identification the author may still have questions about the properties of the plant. Information about toxicity and edibility has to be separated from a guess at the species from a photograph and backed by a verifiable source.

scenarios.name: The first-time houseplant owner
scenarios.job: Hires the app to finally not kill their first ficus at home: what is needed is one simple “water it now” signal, with no encyclopedias or subscriptions.
scenarios.gap: A beginner needs to be able to move a reminder and to mark a watering clearly. Requests for complex reports on a plant’s condition can get in the way of that short job.
